newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Asia seen Australian wine industry challenge.
newsitem.headline: Asia seen Australian wine industry challenge.

text.p: The Australian wine industry's immediate challenge was to establish a foothold in Asia without compromising its drive into Europe and North America, the Australian Wine Export Council (AWEC) said on Friday.

AWEC international manager Kevin O'Brien said in a statement markets in both Hong Kong and China had grown more than 100 percent in 1996/97, albeit from small bases, with the value of exports to Hong Kong at A$11 million and to China at A$6 million.
"Chinese wine consumers are increasingly choosing wine in preference to higher strength liquor," he said.
"If this trend continues, and we believe it will, it presents an enormous opportunity for the Australian wine industry," he said.

O'Brien said that with the total value of Australian wine exports for the fiscal year confirmed at A$596 million, export volumes to the United Kingdom, Australia's largest market, were up 19 percent to 72.7 million litres with value up 22 percent to A$257 million.
The value of exports to the United States was up 56 percent to A$120 million, with volume rising 43 percent to 22.7 million litres, he said. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
